scope.covers: Leitura para compreensão global e identificação de tese, propósito, ideias principais e relações entre ideias; seleção, hierarquização e condensação de informações; diferença entre resumo, paráfrase e citação; reelaboração em inglês com vocabulário e estrutura próprios, preservação do sentido e dos limites do texto-base; organização de parágrafo, coesão, conectores, referência pronominal e progressão temática; correção gramatical, lexical, ortográfica e de registro; revisão de fidelidade, concisão e clareza.
scope.excludes: Tradução integral, crítica ou opinião pessoal sobre o texto-base, produção de ensaio argumentativo independente, regras de citação de um estilo bibliográfico específico e análise literária especializada.

theoryTitle: Compreender, sintetizar e reelaborar em inglês

chapters.title: 1. Compreender e selecionar as ideias
chapters.markdown:
### O problema que este assunto resolve

Um resumo correto começa antes da escrita: é preciso entender o texto inteiro e separar o que sustenta sua mensagem do que apenas ilustra ou detalha. A primeira frase nem sempre apresenta a tese; uma ressalva no final pode limitar uma afirmação anterior. Ler só palavras isoladas e copiá-las produz um mosaico, não uma síntese.

> **Siglas e termos deste capítulo**
> - **Main idea**: ideia central que organiza o texto ou um parágrafo.
> - **Supporting detail**: dado, exemplo, causa ou explicação que sustenta uma ideia.
> - **Thesis/claim**: posição ou afirmação principal defendida pelo autor.
> - **Scope**: limites do que o texto afirma, como população, período ou condição.

### Leitura em duas passagens

Na primeira leitura, identifique tema, propósito e direção geral: informar, explicar um processo, comparar opções ou defender uma tese. Na segunda, anote a função de cada parágrafo e marque relações como causa e efeito, contraste, condição e conclusão. Observe marcadores: **however** costuma introduzir contraste; **because** apresenta causa; **therefore** sinaliza consequência; **for example** introduz ilustração. O marcador orienta a leitura, mas a relação precisa ser confirmada pelo conteúdo.

| Elemento | Pergunta útil | Tratamento no resumo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tese ou mensagem central | O que o autor quer explicar ou sustentar? | Preservar, se central |
| Razão principal | Por que a tese é apresentada? | Manter se sustenta a mensagem |
| Exemplo isolado | Que caso concreto ilustra a ideia? | Em geral, condensar ou omitir |
| Ressalva | Em que condição a afirmação deixa de valer? | Manter quando altera o alcance |
| Repetição | Que ideia já foi expressa? | Fundir sem apagar ênfase relevante |

### Da leitura às notas

Feche o texto ou afaste-o por um momento e formule uma frase que responda “What is the text mainly saying?”. Depois registre poucas palavras-chave por ideia, sem copiar frases inteiras. Confira cada nota no original: uma causa não pode virar consequência; “some” não pode virar “all”; uma previsão não pode ser apresentada como fato consumado. Se o texto compara duas alternativas, anote ambas e o critério da comparação.

A hierarquia ajuda a decidir o que cortar. Nomes, datas, números e exemplos ficam quando são indispensáveis para a mensagem ou quando o comando os exige. Detalhes repetidos, comentários laterais e ilustrações geralmente cedem espaço. O resumo deve ser substancialmente mais curto que o texto-fonte, mas não há uma proporção universal: extensão e tarefa determinam o nível de detalhe.

### Como cai na prova

- Uma alternativa que transforma “may reduce” em “will eliminate” exagera certeza e efeito.
- Um resumo que guarda um exemplo chamativo e omite a tese não representa o texto.
- Uma ressalva como “in small trials” limita a afirmação; removê-la pode torná-la falsa.
- “For example” indica função ilustrativa; não torna automaticamente o exemplo a ideia principal.

chapters.title: 2. Resumo, paráfrase e reelaboração
chapters.markdown:
### O problema que este assunto resolve

Síntese e reelaboração são operações relacionadas, mas não iguais. O resumo comunica o núcleo do texto com grande condensação; a paráfrase reexpressa uma passagem ou ideia específica com mais detalhe. Em ambas, a redação deve ser própria e o sentido do original deve continuar reconhecível. Trocar alguns substantivos por sinônimos, mantendo a mesma sequência e construção, é uma paráfrase fraca e pode reproduzir linguagem alheia de perto.

> **Siglas e termos deste capítulo**
> - **Summary**: versão bem mais curta que retém as ideias centrais.
> - **Paraphrase**: reformulação detalhada de uma ideia com palavras e estrutura diferentes.
> - **Quotation**: reprodução literal, assinalada como citação quando a tarefa permite.
> - **Patchwriting**: cópia da estrutura ou de fragmentos com substituições superficiais.

### O que muda entre as três formas

| Forma | Quanto conserva | Linguagem | Uso típico |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Citação | Palavras exatas do autor | Literal e delimitada | Quando a formulação original importa |
| Paráfrase | Conteúdo específico em detalhe | Nova formulação e estrutura | Explicar uma passagem relevante |
| Resumo | Ideias principais, com menos detalhe | Nova formulação, muito condensada | Dar visão geral do texto |

Um resumo não é uma sequência de frases copiadas, nem uma avaliação. Uma paráfrase pode ser tão longa quanto o trecho original, pois mantém mais detalhes; um resumo deve reduzir bastante o conteúdo. Em trabalho acadêmico, a fonte deve ser atribuída também quando se resume ou parafraseia. Em uma prova de compreensão, siga as instruções do enunciado sobre referência e formato.

### Como reelaborar sem distorcer

Leia uma unidade de sentido, identifique sua proposição e a relação lógica, depois escreva sem olhar para a formulação original. Mude a construção sintática e escolha palavras adequadas, não sinônimos mecânicos. Reabra o original e compare: agentes, ações, polaridade, modalidade, tempo, condição, comparação e grau de certeza precisam continuar iguais. Termos técnicos importantes podem permanecer; não há obrigação de substituir toda palavra.

Exemplo autoral: “The new route may shorten the trip, but it does not serve the northern district.” Uma síntese fiel seria “The route may reduce travel time, although the northern district remains unserved.” Ela preserva a possibilidade, não promete resultado; preserva também a limitação territorial. “The route will make travel faster for everyone” altera certeza e alcance.

Não acrescente opinião, recomendação ou explicação que não esteja sustentada pelo texto. Se a tarefa pede resumo, atribuir uma intenção não declarada ou discordar do autor desloca o foco. A concisão não autoriza omitir uma condição que muda a conclusão.

### Como cai na prova

- Paráfrase mantém mais conteúdo específico que o resumo, mas muda vocabulário e estrutura.
- Um resumo combina as ideias centrais; não precisa reproduzir cada etapa ou exemplo.
- Substituir “increase” por “rise” sem alterar a frase pode manter cópia estrutural.
- Opinião do candidato, citação extensa ou informação externa não solicitada não pertence à síntese.

chapters.title: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês
chapters.markdown:
### O problema que este assunto resolve

Mesmo com ideias corretas, um resumo pode ficar difícil de acompanhar se as frases não mostrarem como uma informação se liga à seguinte. Coesão em inglês depende de relações lógicas claras, referência pronominal identificável e progressão de uma ideia para outra. Conectores não são enfeites: cada um compromete o escritor com uma relação específica.

> **Siglas e termos deste capítulo**
> - **Cohesion**: ligações linguísticas explícitas entre partes do texto.
> - **Coherence**: sequência de ideias que faz sentido como conjunto.
> - **Reference**: expressão, como pronome, que retoma ou antecipa outra informação.
> - **Transition/linker**: palavra ou expressão que sinaliza uma relação lógica.

### Escolher conectores pelo sentido

| Relação | Conectores frequentes | Exemplo de função |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adição | **also, furthermore** | Acrescentar ponto compatível |
| Contraste/concessão | **however, although, whereas** | Mostrar diferença ou ressalva |
| Causa | **because, since** | Apresentar razão |
| Resultado | **therefore, consequently** | Apresentar efeito ou conclusão |
| Exemplo | **for example, such as** | Ilustrar uma categoria |
| Sequência | **first, then, finally** | Ordenar etapas |

**Although** introduz uma concessão e normalmente integra uma oração subordinada; **however** funciona como advérbio de transição e precisa de pontuação apropriada. **Because** indica causa, não resultado. **Therefore** não deve ser usado para introduzir uma evidência que apenas exemplifica. Uma relação errada pode contradizer o conteúdo embora cada frase, isoladamente, esteja gramatical.

### Referência e progressão

Em “The policy supports local clinics because they serve remote communities”, **they** retoma **local clinics**. Se houver dois antecedentes possíveis, repita o substantivo. Pronomes como **it**, **they** e **this** devem apontar claramente para uma entidade ou ideia; **this trend** é mais preciso que um **this** solto quando há várias afirmações anteriores. Evite iniciar cada frase com “The text says”: o resumo deve expor a mensagem, não narrar continuamente o ato de resumir.

Um parágrafo curto costuma funcionar com uma frase de abertura que declara o tema e a conclusão principal, seguida por razões ou relações indispensáveis. A ordem pode ser reorganizada, desde que preserve a lógica. Combine frases relacionadas quando isso melhora a leitura, sem produzir períodos longos e ambíguos. Uma boa sequência responde: qual é a mensagem, que apoio essencial ela recebe e que limite ou resultado precisa ser registrado?

### Como cai na prova

- Se a segunda frase contradiz a primeira, **however** pode ser adequado; **therefore** não.
- Um pronome com dois antecedentes plausíveis cria ambiguidade mesmo que concorde em número.
- Conector de resultado não substitui o de causa: compare “because” e “therefore”.
- A ordem de apresentação pode mudar, mas causa, contraste e condição precisam permanecer fiéis.

chapters.title: 4. Inglês correto e revisão final
chapters.markdown:
### O problema que este assunto resolve

A versão final precisa ser simultaneamente fiel e legível. Erros pequenos de tempo verbal, concordância, artigo, preposição ou escolha lexical podem mudar quem fez algo, quando aconteceu ou com que grau de certeza. Revisar somente ortografia não basta: é necessário testar sentido, gramática, vocabulário e concisão.

> **Siglas e termos deste capítulo**
> - **Tense**: forma verbal que situa evento ou estado no tempo.
> - **Agreement**: concordância, por exemplo, sujeito singular com verbo singular no presente.
> - **Register**: nível de formalidade e escolha de linguagem para a tarefa.
> - **Proofreading**: revisão final de forma, clareza e erros mecânicos.

### Pontos gramaticais que mudam o sentido

No presente simples, a terceira pessoa singular recebe **-s**: “The report **shows** a decline”; “The reports **show** a decline”. Com o auxiliar **does**, o verbo principal volta à forma-base: “The report **does show**”, não “does shows”. O passado regular costuma receber **-ed**, mas verbos irregulares têm formas próprias; mantenha a cronologia indicada no original em vez de converter todo texto para o presente.

Artigos também carregam informação. Um substantivo contável singular normalmente requer determinante: “a result”, “the result”. Plurais genéricos podem aparecer sem artigo: “Results vary”. **Some**, **many**, **most** e **all** não são intercambiáveis; conservar quantificadores evita generalizações indevidas. Compare ainda modalização: **may** indica possibilidade, **must** necessidade ou forte inferência, e **should** recomendação ou expectativa.

Use vocabulário idiomático e preciso. **Affect** costuma funcionar como verbo (“The change affects access”); **effect**, como substantivo (“the effect of the change”), embora existam usos menos comuns. Evite falsos cognatos e traduções palavra por palavra. Inglês correto não significa usar palavras raras: significa selecionar uma forma natural que exprima a relação original.

### Revisão em quatro passagens

1. **Fidelidade**: cada afirmação pode ser localizada no texto-base? Preserve negações, ressalvas, números solicitados e autoria das ações.
2. **Síntese**: ficaram tese e apoios necessários? Há exemplo ou repetição que pode sair?
3. **Língua**: confira sujeito-verbo, tempo, artigos, pronomes, conectores, ortografia e pontuação.
4. **Leitura final**: leia o resumo sozinho. Ele é claro, coeso, curto e adequado ao registro pedido?

A revisão deve comparar o resumo com o original e também lê-lo como texto independente. Uma frase gramatical pode estar infiel; uma seleção fiel pode estar escrita com erro. As duas verificações são necessárias.

### Como cai na prova

- “Most residents” não equivale a “all residents”; quantificadores preservam o alcance.
- “The data show” pede verbo plural na variedade formal padrão; “the result shows” é singular.
- “May increase” não autoriza escrever “increases” como certeza.
- A resposta melhor é a que combina sentido preservado, síntese e inglês claro, não a que apenas repete palavras do texto.

summary: Para resumir em inglês, compreenda o texto inteiro, identifique tese e relações entre ideias, hierarquize informações e retenha o que sustenta a mensagem. O resumo é muito mais condensado que a paráfrase; ambos reformulam com palavras próprias e preservam sentido, ressalvas, agentes e grau de certeza, sem acrescentar opinião ou informação externa. Organize as ideias com conectores adequados e referências claras. Revise fidelidade, concisão, gramática, vocabulário, ortografia e registro.

flashcards.front: What is the main purpose of a summary?
flashcards.back: To present the source's central message and essential supporting ideas in a substantially shorter form.

flashcards.front: How does a paraphrase differ from a summary?
flashcards.back: A paraphrase restates a specific idea in more detail; a summary selects and condenses the main points of a larger text.

flashcards.front: What must a faithful summary preserve?
flashcards.back: The source's meaning, logical relations, scope, qualifications, and degree of certainty.

flashcards.front: What should usually happen to a minor example in a summary?
flashcards.back: It is omitted or compressed unless it is necessary to understand the central point or the prompt requires it.

flashcards.front: What does however normally signal?
flashcards.back: Contrast or a qualification that complicates the preceding point.

flashcards.front: What relation does therefore signal?
flashcards.back: A result or conclusion, rather than a cause or a mere example.

flashcards.front: What does because introduce?
flashcards.back: A cause or reason.

flashcards.front: What does although introduce?
flashcards.back: A concessive clause: an idea that contrasts with, but does not cancel, the main clause.

flashcards.front: Why is may important to preserve?
flashcards.back: It marks possibility; replacing it with will or a bare present can overstate certainty.

flashcards.front: Why can most not be replaced by all?
flashcards.back: Most allows exceptions; all makes a universal claim and changes the scope.

flashcards.front: What is patchwriting?
flashcards.back: Keeping the source's wording or sentence pattern while making only superficial substitutions.

flashcards.front: Can a technical term remain in a paraphrase?
flashcards.back: Yes. A necessary technical term may remain; the rest should be genuinely reformulated.

flashcards.front: What does a clear pronoun reference require?
flashcards.back: A reader can identify its antecedent without choosing among multiple plausible nouns or ideas.

flashcards.front: What is a useful first reading goal?
flashcards.back: Identify the topic, purpose, overall message, and direction of the text.

flashcards.front: What should the second reading examine?
flashcards.back: Paragraph functions and relations such as cause, contrast, condition, evidence, and conclusion.

flashcards.front: How should a summary treat the writer's opinion?
flashcards.back: It should report the source's position without adding the summarizer's judgment unless asked to evaluate.

flashcards.front: What is the present simple form for a singular third-person subject?
flashcards.back: The lexical verb normally takes -s or -es: the report shows.

flashcards.front: What form follows does in a question or emphasis?
flashcards.back: The base verb: does the report show; the report does show.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between affect and effect in common use?
flashcards.back: Affect is commonly a verb; effect is commonly a noun.

flashcards.front: What are the four final review checks?
flashcards.back: Fidelity, selection and concision, English form, and clarity as a standalone text.

tips: After the first full reading, state the text's message in one plain English sentence before drafting.
Use brief notes for each paragraph's function; avoid copying complete sentences into the notes.
Keep a qualifier such as may, some, mainly, or in small trials when it limits the claim.
Choose each linker for its logical relation, then check that the following clause fulfills it.
When a pronoun could refer to two nouns, repeat the intended noun instead.
Compare the finished summary with the source, then read the summary once without the source for flow.
traps: A paraphrase is not made original by replacing a few words while retaining the source's sentence frame.
A vivid example may attract attention but still be less important than the author's general claim.
Shortening a sentence by deleting its condition can turn a qualified claim into a false universal.
However and therefore do different jobs: contrast is not the same relation as consequence.
A grammatical sentence can still distort who acted, what happened, or how certain the source was.
Adding a sensible opinion or background fact does not make it part of a source-based summary.

activeRecall.question: Describe a two-pass method for reading a text before writing its summary.
activeRecall.answer: First identify topic, purpose, and overall message. Then mark each paragraph's role and the logical relations among the central ideas, checking qualifications and scope.

activeRecall.question: Explain why a summary is usually shorter than a paraphrase.
activeRecall.answer: A summary selects the source's main points and removes most supporting detail; a paraphrase restates a particular idea more fully.

activeRecall.question: How can you detect patchwriting in your draft?
activeRecall.answer: Compare sentence order, phrasing, and syntax with the source. If only a few words changed while the source's frame remains, rewrite from understood notes.

activeRecall.question: What information can a small qualifier carry?
activeRecall.answer: It can limit certainty, population, time, or conditions. Removing it may make a claim broader or stronger than the source.

activeRecall.question: When is however a better connector than therefore?
activeRecall.answer: When the next point contrasts with or qualifies the previous one; therefore is for a result or conclusion.

activeRecall.question: How do you resolve an ambiguous pronoun?
activeRecall.answer: Identify its intended antecedent and repeat a precise noun phrase if readers could reasonably attach it to another antecedent.

activeRecall.question: Name four language features to inspect during final revision.
activeRecall.answer: Subject–verb agreement, tense, articles and countability, and accurate connectors; also check pronouns, spelling, punctuation, and register.

activeRecall.question: Why are source comparison and standalone reading both needed?
activeRecall.answer: Comparison tests fidelity; standalone reading tests whether the compressed text is clear and coherent without relying on the original.

errorConcepts.title: Summary confused with paraphrase
errorConcepts.summary: A summary selects and condenses the central message; a paraphrase restates a particular idea in greater detail. Both require genuine reformulation.

errorConcepts.title: Qualifier or scope erased
errorConcepts.summary: Words such as may, some, most, and under certain conditions constrain claims. Removing or strengthening them distorts the source.

errorConcepts.title: Connector chosen by appearance
errorConcepts.summary: Because marks a reason, therefore a result, whereas/however a contrast, and for example an illustration. Choose by the actual relation.

errorConcepts.title: Surface-level paraphrase
errorConcepts.summary: Synonym replacement alone may preserve copied syntax and phrasing. Understand the idea, write from notes, and compare meaning afterward.

errorConcepts.title: Faithfulness mistaken for grammatical correctness
errorConcepts.summary: A fluent sentence may still change tense, agent, certainty, quantity, or causality. Review language and fidelity separately.

questions.statement: A text says that a pilot program may reduce delays at two rural clinics, although the trial lasted only one month. Which summary preserves both the claim and its limits?

options.text: The program eliminated delays at every clinic after a successful year-long trial.
A short trial suggests the program may reduce delays at two rural clinics.
The trial proves rural clinics need a permanent national program.
The program caused delays, although the clinics received additional staff.
All clinics reduced delays because the pilot lasted several months.

questions.explanation: A short trial involving two clinics supports only a tentative, limited conclusion. The selected summary keeps may and the study's scope; the other versions invent certainty, duration, outcomes, or coverage.

questions.statement: In a source-based summary, which action best demonstrates synthesis rather than copying?

options.text: Copy one sentence from each paragraph and remove its opening phrase.
Replace selected nouns with synonyms but keep each sentence's structure.
List every example in its original order to preserve all details.
Combine central claims in new wording.
Add background information so the summary can stand without the source.

questions.explanation: Synthesis selects and combines the text's central ideas in a new, shorter formulation. Sentence copying, synonym swaps, exhaustive example lists, and outside additions do not accomplish that task.

questions.statement: A paragraph ends: ‘The device is inexpensive. However, its battery lasts only two hours.’ What relation does however express?

options.text: The second sentence gives a consequence of the low price.
The second sentence introduces an example of the device.
It contrasts with or qualifies the earlier advantage.
The second sentence explains the cause of the device's price.
The second sentence restates the first point in more precise terms.

questions.explanation: However signals contrast. The short battery life limits the positive assessment based on price; it is not presented as a cause, result, example, or restatement.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: Which revision correctly completes the sentence ‘The report ___ a decline in bus use’?

options.text: show
showing
have shown
are showing
shows

questions.explanation: The singular third-person subject ‘the report’ takes ‘shows’ in the present simple. The other choices either lack agreement or require a different grammatical construction.

questions.statement: A source says that some residents opposed the plan. Which sentence preserves its quantity?

options.text: Some residents opposed the plan.
All residents opposed the plan.
No residents opposed the plan.
Most residents opposed the plan unanimously.
Every resident rejected the plan for the same reason.

questions.explanation: Some preserves the limited, unspecified quantity. All, no, most, and every make different claims; unanimity and a common reason are also unsupported.

questions.statement: Which sentence is the best concise summary of a text arguing that urban trees cool streets, absorb rainwater, and require maintenance?

options.text: Every city should plant trees immediately because trees solve climate change.
Urban trees provide cooling and help manage rain, but they need care.
A tree planted near one street absorbed rain during a storm last year.
The author personally prefers green neighborhoods to paved streets.
Cities have many trees, and their branches and roots require attention.

questions.explanation: The best option condenses all three central points: cooling, rainwater management, and maintenance. The others add a policy or climate claim, focus on one example, invent an opinion, or omit the benefits.

questions.statement: Which sentence uses because to express the relation in ‘The match was postponed because heavy rain flooded the field’?

options.text: Heavy rain flooded the field because the match was postponed.
The match was postponed; therefore, heavy rain began.
The field flooded, for example, the match was postponed.
The match was postponed because heavy rain flooded the field.
Although the rain flooded the field, the match was postponed because it ended.

questions.explanation: Because introduces the reason for postponement: flooding from heavy rain. The distractors reverse cause and effect or use connectors that do not express the stated relation.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: Which rewrite best paraphrases ‘The council reduced opening hours because energy costs rose’?

options.text: The council reduced opening hours because energy costs rose.
Energy costs rose, and the council may expand its hours.
The council shortened its schedule in response to higher energy expenses.
The council reduced energy costs because opening hours rose.
The council's decision had no connection with energy prices.

questions.explanation: The rewrite changes wording and structure while preserving the council's action and the cost increase as its reason. The original itself is not a reformulation, and the other choices reverse or deny the stated relation.

questions.statement: A source states: ‘The new service may reach smaller towns.’ Which version preserves the source's degree of certainty?

options.text: The service has already reached every small town.
The service will certainly reach all towns.
The service never reaches towns with small populations.
The service reached smaller towns in the past.
The service could become available in smaller towns.

questions.explanation: Could preserves possibility, and smaller towns retains the limited scope. Certainty, universal coverage, negation, or a past event is not stated in the source.

questions.statement: What is the most reliable way to identify a text's central message before drafting?

options.text: Read the title only and infer what the author probably intended.
Copy the first sentence and treat it as the thesis in every text.
Select the longest paragraph and omit the rest of the text.
Read the whole text, note its purpose, and connect the central points.
Count repeated words without checking how the argument develops.

questions.explanation: The message emerges from the whole text and the roles its ideas play. Titles, opening sentences, paragraph length, and repeated words may help, but none alone reliably establishes the thesis.

questions.statement: In ‘The library extended its hours. This allowed evening students to borrow books,’ what does this refer to most clearly?

options.text: The library's extension of its opening hours.
The books that evening students borrowed.
The students' decision to study in the evening.
A separate library building mentioned earlier.
The number of books held by the library.

questions.explanation: This refers to the preceding action of extending library hours, which made borrowing possible in the evening. The other options are not the action described as enabling access.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: Which draft avoids adding the summarizer's personal judgment?

options.text: The author correctly proves that the proposed timetable is unfair.
The timetable is obviously a poor choice for every school.
In my view, the new schedule should be rejected without delay.
The proposal is foolish, although some readers may support it.
The author argues that the schedule would reduce morning congestion.

questions.explanation: The final option reports the author's position without endorsing or criticizing it. The others add evaluation, certainty, or the summarizer's recommendation.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly completes ‘The reports ___ that access improved after the change’?

options.text: shows
show
showing
does shows
is show

questions.explanation: Reports is plural, so the present simple verb is show. Shows agrees with a singular subject, while the other forms are incomplete or ungrammatical here.

questions.statement: A text says that most surveyed workers preferred flexible schedules. Which summary is faithful?

options.text: Every worker prefers flexible schedules in every workplace.
No workers supported fixed schedules in the survey.
A majority of surveyed workers favored flexible schedules.
Workers rejected all scheduling choices except remote work.
Flexible schedules increased productivity for the surveyed workers.

questions.explanation: A majority accurately restates most, and surveyed workers preserves the population studied. The other options make universal claims, add results or choices, or reverse the finding.

questions.statement: Which plan is best for revising a short summary after its first draft?

options.text: Check fidelity, trim detail, and review English and flow.
Add examples and opinions first, then correct spelling if time remains.
Replace every repeated word with a rare synonym regardless of meaning.
Compare only the first sentence with the original and keep the rest.
Shorten every sentence by deleting conditions and transition words.

questions.explanation: Revision should test whether claims match the source, whether the selection is concise, and whether the English is clear and correct. The other approaches risk unsupported content, inaccurate vocabulary, or unreviewed distortion.

questions.statement: A summary should retain every example and supporting detail from the source to remain faithful.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Errado. A summary is substantially condensed and normally selects central points rather than retaining every example. A detail remains only when needed to preserve the message or when the prompt requests it.

questions.statement: A paraphrase can preserve a technical term when that term is necessary to express the source's idea accurately.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Certo. Reformulation requires new wording and structure, not forced replacement of every word. A precise technical term may remain when it is the clearest name for the concept.

questions.statement: If a text says that a treatment may help some patients, a summary can state that it cures all patients as long as the sentence is shorter.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Errado. Shortness does not excuse changing modality or scope. May help some patients is tentative and limited; cures all patients is certain and universal.

questions.statement: The connector therefore normally introduces a reason that explains why an earlier event occurred.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Errado. Therefore usually signals a result or conclusion that follows from an earlier point. Because or since commonly introduces the reason or cause that explains an event.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: A clear summary can omit a minor illustration while retaining the claim that the illustration was used to support.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Certo. Summaries select main ideas and often omit particular examples. The claim and its essential qualification should remain understandable after compression.

questions.statement: Changing only a few nouns while retaining the source's sentence pattern is always enough to make a paraphrase original.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Errado. Superficial synonym changes can leave the source's phrasing and structure intact. A sound paraphrase expresses the understood idea through genuinely different wording and syntax.

questions.statement: In the present simple, a singular third-person subject normally takes a verb ending in -s or -es.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Certo. Standard present-simple forms include ‘the report shows’ and ‘the policy changes’. Plural subjects take the base form: ‘reports show’.

questions.statement: The word however usually marks contrast or qualification between nearby ideas.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Certo. However signals that the next point contrasts with or qualifies what came before; punctuation must also suit its position in the sentence.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: A summary should add the writer's evaluation so the reader knows whether the original argument is convincing.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Errado. A summary reports the source's main ideas without adding the summarizer's judgment. Evaluation belongs only when the task separately asks for critique.

questions.statement: The pronoun this is always clear even when several events or claims appear in the preceding sentence.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Errado. A pronoun must have an identifiable antecedent. When several candidates are present, name the intended event or idea, such as ‘this change’ or ‘this result’.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: Reading the whole text before selecting details helps prevent an example from being mistaken for the central claim.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Certo. The function of a detail is clearer when read in the context of the whole argument. A vivid case may illustrate rather than define the main message.

questions.statement: A polished and grammatical sentence cannot distort the source's meaning.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Errado. Fluency does not guarantee fidelity. A sentence can be grammatical while reversing cause and effect, changing a quantity, or making a tentative claim certain.

questions.statement: A paraphrase may be as long as or longer than the source passage because it preserves more detail than a summary.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Certo. A paraphrase reexpresses a specific passage in detail and need not be shorter. A summary, by contrast, selects and condenses central points.

questions.statement: The connector for example usually introduces a cause that produces the preceding claim.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Errado. For example introduces an illustration or instance. It does not by itself state the cause of the preceding idea.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: Changing may to will can strengthen a claim beyond what the source supports.

options.text: Certo
Errado

questions.explanation: Certo. May expresses possibility, while will commonly presents an expected or future event more definitely. A summary should preserve the source's degree of certainty.

questions.statement: Which paraphrase best restates ‘Although the road is shorter, it is often closed in winter’?

options.text: The road is shorter, so it remains open throughout winter.
The road is often closed in winter because it is shorter.
Despite its shorter route, the road frequently closes during winter.
The road becomes shorter whenever winter closures begin.
The road is longer, although winter rarely affects its use.

questions.explanation: The correct reformulation preserves concession, relative shortness, and frequent winter closure. The alternatives change the relation, cause, timing, or facts.

questions.statement: A report says that ‘the grant supports projects led by local groups, provided that they publish annual accounts.’ Which summary preserves the condition?

options.text: The grant supports local projects without any reporting requirement.
The grant supports locally led projects if they publish yearly accounts.
The grant requires local groups to fund every public project.
Annual accounts are published only after the grant ends permanently.
The grant supports projects led by national offices that publish monthly accounts.

questions.explanation: Provided that expresses a condition, accurately restated by if. The other versions omit or change the condition, recipient, funding role, or reporting frequency.

questions.statement: A source reports that a survey included 800 adults, but its main finding is that trust rose after public meetings. The prompt asks for a one-sentence summary of the finding. What should be prioritized?

options.text: The sample size alone, because numbers are always the most important detail.
The meeting schedule, even though the text gives no such information.
A claim that meetings caused trust to rise in every community.
The central finding, with any causal limit stated by the source retained.
A list of each participant's response in the original survey order.

questions.explanation: The prompt asks for the main finding, so the summary should foreground it. The sample size may be omitted unless required; the writer must not invent causation or details absent from the source.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly completes ‘The committee does ___ the evidence before making a recommendation’?

options.text: reviews
reviewed
reviewing
has reviews
review

questions.explanation: After the auxiliary does, the main verb takes its base form: review. The third-person marking is already carried by does, so ‘does reviews’ is incorrect.

questions.statement: Which two-sentence summary is most coherent for a source stating that online forms save processing time, but users without internet access still need in-person assistance?

options.text: Online forms can speed processing. However, people without internet access still need in-person help.
Online forms speed processing. Therefore, people without internet access need no assistance.
People need in-person assistance. For example, online forms always save time.
Online forms save time because users without internet access receive assistance.
All users can use online forms, although no processing time changes.

questions.explanation: The first sentence states the benefit and the second preserves the access limitation with a contrastive connector. The other choices draw an unsupported result, mislabel an example, reverse causality, or contradict the source.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: A source says that the museum opened a new wing in 2022 and that visitor numbers rose afterward. Which sentence avoids claiming an unproven cause?

options.text: The new wing caused every visitor to return to the museum.
Visitor numbers rose after the museum opened a new wing in 2022.
The museum opened its wing because visitors had already increased.
The wing opened in 2022, proving that admission became free.
Visitor numbers fell before the museum built a second museum.

questions.explanation: Afterward establishes sequence, not necessarily causation. The faithful option reports the order of events without asserting that the new wing caused the increase or adding unsupported facts.

questions.statement: Which revision best fixes the unclear reference in ‘The school changed its bus route after the city revised its schedule. This caused complaints’?

options.text: This happened after that, and it caused complaints from them.
The school changed it after the city revised that, which caused them.
The change caused the complaints.
The revised city schedule caused complaints about the school route.
There were complaints after some changes were made somewhere.

questions.explanation: The original ‘this’ could refer to either the route change or the city's schedule revision. Naming the revised schedule makes the intended cause explicit; other choices preserve or worsen ambiguity or omit the facts.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: A text says that a policy reduced costs in two pilot hospitals, while its effect on smaller clinics remains unknown. Which summary is faithful?

options.text: The policy reduced costs in all hospitals, including smaller clinics.
The policy failed to reduce costs in the pilot hospitals.
The policy lowered costs in two pilot hospitals; its effect on smaller clinics is unknown.
Smaller clinics proved the policy lowers costs throughout the health system.
The policy will reduce costs in every clinic once it is expanded.

questions.explanation: The correct version retains the observed result, the two-hospital scope, and uncertainty about smaller clinics. The alternatives generalize, reverse the result, or turn an unknown future effect into proof.

questions.statement: Which wording is most appropriate for a concise formal summary of a report that says an agency examined complaints and found a recurring delay?

options.text: The agency looked into complaints and found that things were kind of slow.
The agency examined complaints and identified a recurring delay.
The agency totally nailed the fact that everything was a mess.
The agency, which is great, discovered the world's worst delay.
The agency examined complaints and proved deliberate misconduct by all staff.

questions.explanation: The selected sentence is concise, neutral, and precise, matching the reported finding. The alternatives are too informal or evaluative, or add an unsupported accusation and exaggerated scope.

questions.statement: Which paraphrase of ‘Although the data are limited, the pattern suggests a gradual decline’ preserves both qualification and certainty?

options.text: The complete data prove that the decline has ended suddenly.
The pattern proves a sharp decline despite extensive data.
Limited information rules out any gradual change.
The decline is gradual because the data are complete.
Despite the small dataset, the trend points to a slow decrease.

questions.explanation: Despite the small dataset preserves limited evidence; points to retains the tentative force of suggests; and slow decrease restates gradual decline. The other choices change the evidence or overstate the conclusion.

questions.statement: Which revision best corrects the grammar in ‘The results shows that each option have a different cost’?

options.text: The results show that each option has a different cost.
The results shows that each option have different costs.
The result show that each options has a different cost.
The results showing that each option having different cost.
The results does show each option have different cost.

questions.explanation: Results is plural and takes show. Each option is grammatically singular and takes has. The other revisions retain agreement errors or create incomplete constructions.

questions.statement: A source argues that remote work can reduce commuting, but also says that new employees may need in-person guidance. Which summary best synthesizes both points?

options.text: Remote work eliminates commuting and makes in-person guidance unnecessary for everyone.
New employees require offices, so remote work cannot reduce commuting.
Remote work can cut commuting, while some new employees may still benefit from in-person guidance.
The source recommends ending remote work and requiring all employees to commute.
Commuting improves guidance, and remote work increases commuting for new employees.

questions.explanation: The correct option combines the benefit and qualification, preserving can and may rather than making either universal. The others erase a point, invert a relation, or invent a recommendation.

questions.statement: A source states that ‘fewer people used the service after fees increased.’ Which rewrite avoids adding a causal link absent from that wording?

options.text: Higher fees caused every user to abandon the service.
After the fee increase, service use fell, though the sentence alone does not establish why.
Service use fell, so the fees must have been reduced.
The service raised fees because fewer people used it afterward.
Every user stopped using the service before fees changed.

questions.explanation: The source gives sequence but does not explicitly establish causation. The correct version preserves the order and avoids claiming why use fell; the alternatives add, reverse, or contradict causality and scope.

questions.statement: Which revision is the clearest way to avoid the vague reference in ‘The plan and the budget changed. This worried the board’?

options.text: The plan and budget changed, and this and that worried the board.
The board worried the plan when the budget changed.
This worried them after everything had changed.
The board changed the plan and budget because it was worried.
The changes to both the plan and budget worried the board.

questions.explanation: This could refer to either the plan change, the budget change, or both. Naming ‘the changes to both’ resolves the reference and preserves the board as the party that was worried.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses the common distinction between affect and effect?

options.text: The schedule may effect how quickly the forms are processed.
The schedule's affect was visible in the processing time.
The schedule may affect processing time, and its effect can be measured.
The schedule may effects processing time for each form.
The schedule affected by processing time had an affective effect.

questions.explanation: In common usage, affect is the verb meaning influence, while effect is the noun meaning result. The selected sentence uses both in those roles; the alternatives misuse their forms or meanings.

questions.statement: A source says that a city tested three bus routes and found that one reduced travel time, while two showed no clear change. Which summary is accurate?

options.text: Testing three routes produced mixed results: one reduced travel time, while two showed no clear change.
All three routes reduced travel time after the city tested its buses.
Two routes reduced travel time, and the third made every trip longer.
The city proved that bus routes never affect travel times.
One route showed no change, while two reduced travel time equally.

questions.explanation: The summary accurately retains the mixed distribution of outcomes and the uncertainty in ‘no clear change.’ The distractors alter how many routes improved or add findings not reported.

questions.statement: Which revision makes the contrast in ‘The app is easy to install. It requires technical support to operate’ explicit without changing the claims?

options.text: The app is easy to install; therefore, technical support is required to operate it.
Although the app is easy to install, operating it requires technical support.
The app is easy to install because technical support operates it.
The app requires support to install, but it operates without assistance.
For example, the app is easy to install and technical support is optional.

questions.explanation: Although marks the contrast between easy installation and support-dependent operation while preserving both facts. The other connectors imply a different relation or reverse the claims.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: Which summary best represents a passage whose main point is that water restrictions reduced household use, while farms received separate exemptions?

options.text: Restrictions reduced water use across every sector without exception.
Farms reduced household water use by receiving exemptions.
Water restrictions had no effect on household consumption or farms.
Restrictions lowered household use, while farms were treated separately through exemptions.
The passage recommends ending all restrictions and removing every exemption.

questions.explanation: The correct summary preserves the household outcome and the separate treatment of farms. The other versions generalize beyond the stated sector, confuse the relationship, deny the finding, or invent a recommendation.

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly completes ‘Each of the proposals ___ a different approach to recycling’?

options.text: offer
are offering
have offered
offering
offers

questions.explanation: The subject is each, which is singular; the phrase ‘of the proposals’ does not change its number. The present-simple verb is therefore offers.

questions.statement: A text says a school introduced smaller classes, after which attendance rose; it does not assess other possible causes. Which summary remains within that evidence?

options.text: Smaller classes were the sole cause of higher attendance at the school.
Attendance rose after smaller classes were introduced, though other causes were not assessed.
Attendance caused the school to introduce larger classes.
The school proved smaller classes always increase attendance everywhere.
Attendance remained unchanged when the school altered class size.

questions.explanation: The selected version reports the sequence and the stated limit without upgrading temporal order to a proven sole cause or a universal result. The distractors invent or reverse the finding.

questions.statement: Which sentence has the clearest reference and preserves the meaning of ‘Researchers compared two diets. The second contained more fiber, and this improved digestion’?

options.text: Researchers compared two diets, and this improved digestion.
The second diet had more fiber, which improved digestion.
The second diet improved more fiber than digestion.
The researchers contained more fiber and compared digestion.
The first diet improved digestion because it contained less fiber.

questions.explanation: The revised sentence makes the second diet the source of the increased fiber and states the reported effect on digestion. The original this could refer to the comparison or the fiber difference; the other options distort roles or findings.
questions.section: 3. Organizar um resumo coeso em inglês

questions.statement: Which final draft best combines fidelity, synthesis, and correct English for a source stating that local volunteers mapped flood risks, but the map excludes informal settlements?

options.text: Volunteers mapped every flood risk in the city, including all informal settlements.
Informal settlements mapped volunteers because flood risks were excluded.
Local volunteers mapped flood risks, but the map does not cover informal settlements.
The map proves that informal settlements face no flood risk at all.
The city mapped volunteer programs, although floods never affect settlements.

questions.explanation: The correct option reports who mapped what and retains the map's exclusion. The alternatives universalize coverage, confuse agents and objects, or infer that unmapped places have no risk.
